items.prompt: A recovery Region must recreate an application network and IAM configuration consistently. Which approach is strongest?

options.text: Use version-controlled infrastructure as code, parameterize the target Region, deploy through a controlled pipeline, and test the resulting resources.
Take screenshots of the primary console and rebuild from memory during the outage.
Create resources manually once and never record the configuration.
Copy only the application binary; network and IAM are implicit.

feedback.Reason: Versioned infrastructure as code makes recovery configuration reproducible and reviewable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation templates and parameters describe resources and dependencies so a target environment can be created consistently.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team validates templates, deploys to the target Region, checks outputs and permissions, and exercises the recovery path.
Details.errorCorrection: Screenshots and undocumented manual work are incomplete, and binaries cannot recreate network or authorization dependencies.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Templates need regional parameters, secrets handling, quota planning, and testing to be truly portable.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Screenshots are not executable or complete configuration.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Unrecorded manual state cannot be reliably reproduced.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Application artifacts do not define infrastructure dependencies.

items.prompt: A team must review the impact of a production infrastructure change before execution. Which CloudFormation capability fits?
constraints: The stack is managed by CloudFormation.

options.text: Create and review a change set, confirm replacements and dependency effects, then execute it through the approved process.
Update the stack directly and inspect the result afterward.
Delete the stack and recreate it to reveal changes.
Change resources in the console without updating the template.

feedback.Reason: Change sets show the proposed resource operations before a stack update is executed.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A change set previews additions, modifications, replacements, and deletions based on the new template and parameters.
Details.scenarioApplication: Operators review the set, protect data resources, schedule the change, and execute with rollback and validation.
Details.errorCorrection: Direct updates discover impact too late, delete-and-recreate is destructive, and console edits create drift.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A change set is a preview, not a guarantee that runtime behavior or quotas will be safe.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Post-change inspection cannot prevent an unsafe replacement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Stack deletion risks data and availability.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Console edits bypass the declared source of truth.

items.prompt: A console change altered a security group managed by CloudFormation. How should the team detect and correct the discrepancy?
constraints: The stack remains the source of truth.

options.text: Run drift detection, review the difference, restore the template-defined state or update the template intentionally, and validate the stack.
Ignore the change because CloudFormation will always overwrite it on its own.
Delete the security group without checking dependent resources.
Record the drift only in a chat message.

feedback.Reason: Drift detection exposes out-of-band changes so the canonical template and deployed state can be reconciled deliberately.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation drift detection compares supported resource properties with the expected stack configuration.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner investigates the change, either reverts it through the template or records an approved template update, then retests recovery.
Details.errorCorrection: CloudFormation does not automatically correct every drift, deletion can break dependents, and chat is not an auditable source of truth.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Not every property or resource is fully drift-detectable, so critical controls also need service-level evidence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Drift may persist and affect future updates or recovery.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Deletion can create a larger outage and is not reconciliation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: A chat record lacks controlled configuration and validation.

items.prompt: A platform has separate network, security, and application lifecycles but one very large stack. What is a safer decomposition?
constraints: Shared resources must have clear ownership.

options.text: Use nested or separate stacks with explicit outputs, dependencies, ownership, and lifecycle boundaries that match the architecture.
Duplicate shared resources in every stack to avoid references.
Put all resources into a single larger template.
Remove outputs and rely on copied identifiers in application code.

feedback.Reason: Stack boundaries should reduce blast radius and match ownership without duplicating shared infrastructure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Nested stacks and cross-stack outputs expose stable interfaces and let independently managed layers evolve safely.
Details.scenarioApplication: The network stack owns subnets and routes, security owns controls, and applications consume outputs rather than copying mutable IDs.
Details.errorCorrection: Duplication creates competing resources, one giant stack increases blast radius, and copied identifiers create hidden coupling.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More stacks require dependency and version coordination and must avoid circular references.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Duplicating shared resources creates inconsistent ownership and extra cost.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A larger stack increases update and recovery blast radius.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Copied identifiers become stale and are hard to govern.

items.prompt: An organization must deploy the same baseline roles and logging resources to many accounts and Regions. Which CloudFormation capability fits?

options.text: Use StackSets with controlled account and Region targets, deployment preferences, permissions, and drift or failure monitoring.
Copy templates manually into every account and edit them independently.
Deploy only to the management account and assume resources are inherited.
Use a single VPC peering connection to replicate IAM resources.

feedback.Reason: StackSets manage consistent CloudFormation deployments across multiple accounts and Regions.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: StackSets define a template and target set and can use service-managed or self-managed permissions with deployment controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: The organization rolls out the baseline in waves, handles failures, and validates each target's resources and drift.
Details.errorCorrection: Manual copies drift, management-account resources are not inherited by other accounts, and networking does not replicate IAM.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Multi-account rollout needs permission, quota, dependency, and failure isolation planning.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Independent edits create drift and inconsistent controls.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Organizations do not inherit arbitrary account resources automatically.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: VPC connectivity has no role in creating IAM resources.

items.prompt: A template works in the primary Region but fails in recovery because an AMI and subnet ID are hard-coded. What is the best correction?

options.text: Use validated parameters, mappings, or regional lookups with explicit ownership and preflight validation for the recovery Region.
Hard-code a second set of IDs beside the first without testing the target.
Use the primary Region's AMI in every Region.
Remove the subnet so CloudFormation chooses any network.

feedback.Reason: Regional portability requires explicit, validated inputs for resources whose identifiers and capabilities differ.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation parameters, mappings, and supported lookups can select target-specific values while keeping the template canonical.
Details.scenarioApplication: The pipeline validates AMI ownership, subnet availability, quotas, and security outputs before deployment.
Details.errorCorrection: Untested hard-coded values remain brittle, AMIs are regional, and removing network placement weakens architecture.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Dynamic lookups need stable ownership and can make deployments depend on target state, so outputs should be controlled.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: More hard-coded values do not establish a validated portable contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: AMI identifiers are Region-specific and may not be compatible.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Implicit placement can violate subnet and security requirements.

items.prompt: A stack update would replace a database resource. What should the team do before execution?
constraints: Recovery is required if the update fails.

options.text: Review the replacement, confirm deletion protection and backup or snapshot policy, test the migration path, and execute only with an approved rollback plan.
Accept replacement because CloudFormation always preserves database data.
Disable backups so replacement completes faster.
Update directly and inspect data after the replacement.

feedback.Reason: A resource replacement can affect data and must be treated as a deliberate migration with a recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation update behavior, deletion policies, snapshots, and application migration must be considered before replacing a stateful resource.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner validates backup and restore, chooses retain or snapshot behavior, and schedules a controlled migration.
Details.errorCorrection: CloudFormation does not guarantee preservation of every replacement, removing backups weakens recovery, and post-failure inspection is too late.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Preserving old resources can cost money and leave cleanup work, but data loss risk is higher.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Replacement behavior depends on resource and policy; preservation is not automatic.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Removing backups trades speed for data loss risk.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Direct updates and post-checks do not protect data before replacement.

items.prompt: A deployment pipeline should create recovery infrastructure without granting every pipeline user broad account permissions. Which control helps?

options.text: Use a dedicated CloudFormation execution role with least-privilege permissions, explicit trust, and separate approval for sensitive changes.
Use the root user so every resource can be created.
Embed an administrator access key in the template.
Allow any account principal to assume the deployment role.

feedback.Reason: A scoped execution role separates deployment authority from human or pipeline identity and limits blast radius.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation can assume an execution role whose trust and permissions define what stack operations may do.
Details.scenarioApplication: The organization reviews role policies, target-account trust, change approvals, and CloudTrail evidence for recovery deployments.
Details.errorCorrection: Root and embedded admin keys violate least privilege, and broad trust lets unintended principals deploy.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A narrow role can block a legitimate recovery step, so permissions need tested coverage and monitored exceptions.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Root access is not an appropriate deployment control.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Embedding administrator credentials exposes a high-impact secret.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Unrestricted trust defeats account and pipeline boundaries.

items.prompt: An application stack imports a network stack output that is renamed during a recovery deployment. What should prevent the break?
constraints: Outputs are consumed by other stacks.

options.text: Treat exported outputs as versioned interfaces, change them compatibly, and test dependent stack deployment before retiring the old export.
Rename exports freely because CloudFormation updates every consumer automatically.
Copy the value into application source and delete the export.
Deploy consumers before the network stack exists.

feedback.Reason: Cross-stack exports are contracts and changes can block or break dependent deployments.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Export names and imported values form a dependency interface that must remain available while consumers migrate.
Details.scenarioApplication: The owner adds a new output, updates consumers, validates the target stack, and removes the old contract only after use ends.
Details.errorCorrection: Consumers are not updated by arbitrary renames, copied values drift, and deployment order must respect dependencies.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Compatibility periods add temporary interface management but prevent recovery-time dependency failures.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: CloudFormation does not make arbitrary export renames compatible.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Copied identifiers lose ownership and can become stale.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Consumers cannot safely resolve a missing producer output.

items.prompt: A recovery deployment uses a template that changed after the last successful test. Which control improves reproducibility?
constraints: Templates and application artifacts change independently.
The recovery test must identify what ran.

options.text: Pin and record versioned templates, parameters, artifacts, and dependency versions in the deployment, and retain the prior known-good set.
Always deploy the latest template at recovery time without review.
Use timestamps only for the application and not infrastructure.
Edit the recovery template live until it works.

feedback.Reason: Version pinning makes a recovery deployment identifiable and rollback-capable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A deployment manifest ties infrastructure and application inputs to immutable or reviewable versions.
Details.scenarioApplication: The runbook retrieves a tested manifest, deploys it, records evidence, and promotes newer versions through a separate test.
Details.errorCorrection: Latest-at-incident can introduce untested changes, partial timestamps omit dependencies, and live edits create drift.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Pinned versions require artifact retention and an update process, but reduce recovery uncertainty.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: The latest version may be untested and change recovery behavior.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Infrastructure must be identified as well as application code.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Live editing is not reproducible or reviewable.

items.prompt: A CloudFormation update fails halfway through a recovery environment deployment. Which behavior should be designed and tested?
constraints: The update can create and replace resources.
The stack must not leave hidden partial state.

options.text: Use appropriate rollback or retain policies, inspect stack events, protect stateful resources, and define how to resume or clean up safely.
Delete every resource immediately without checking data or dependencies.
Ignore stack failure because the next deployment will fix it automatically.
Disable rollback for every stack to preserve all partial resources.

feedback.Reason: Failed infrastructure changes need an explicit boundary that protects state and leaves operators with actionable evidence.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Stack events, rollback behavior, deletion or retention policies, and idempotent templates determine how a failed update is recovered.
Details.scenarioApplication: Operators preserve data resources, diagnose the failing event, and either continue, roll back, or clean up according to the runbook.
Details.errorCorrection: Blind deletion can destroy data, ignored failures leave unknown state, and disabling rollback globally increases blast radius.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Retaining failed resources can cost money and require cleanup, but is safer for stateful recovery diagnosis.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Deletion without dependency and data review can worsen the incident.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: A later deployment does not guarantee safe repair of partial state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Rollback policy must be chosen by resource and recovery risk, not disabled globally.

items.prompt: A template references a resource type that is unavailable in the target Region. What should the deployment pipeline do?
constraints: The template is shared across Regions.
Failure should occur before the incident.

options.text: Validate resource availability, quotas, parameters, and dependencies in every target Region before declaring the recovery artifact ready.
Discover the unsupported resource during an outage and substitute a random service.
Remove the resource from the template without checking its purpose.
Assume CloudFormation will emulate unavailable resource types.

feedback.Reason: Regional portability must be validated before the recovery path is needed.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Preflight and deployment tests expose unsupported types, limits, IAM, network, and dependency gaps in the target.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team uses a target-specific parameter or an approved alternative and updates the recovery runbook with evidence.
Details.errorCorrection: Incident-time substitution is untested, removing a resource may break the service, and CloudFormation does not emulate unavailable types.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Target validation adds pipeline work and may require a supported regional architecture variant.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: An outage is not a safe time to invent an untested substitute.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Blind removal can break a required dependency.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: CloudFormation cannot create an unsupported regional resource type.

items.prompt: A recovery stack fails, but the team receives no event history or resource-level reason. Which improvement is needed?
constraints: The stack can be deployed by automation.
Operators need evidence during an outage.

options.text: Publish stack events and deployment logs to the operational system, retain them, and link failures to an owner and runbook.
Suppress failure events so operators see only a final status.
Use screenshots instead of event history.
Retry indefinitely without recording the failed operation.

feedback.Reason: Infrastructure recovery needs observable, retained evidence to locate and correct the failing resource or dependency.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: CloudFormation events and pipeline logs show resource transitions, errors, and ordering that a final status hides.
Details.scenarioApplication: The runbook uses the event identifier to route ownership, repair the template or dependency, and rerun safely.
Details.errorCorrection: Suppressed events remove diagnosis, screenshots are incomplete, and infinite retry can amplify failure.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Log retention and event volume cost money, so retention should match recovery and audit needs.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A final status omits the resource and dependency context.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Screenshots are not a reliable searchable event record.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Retries without evidence can repeat an unsafe failure.

items.prompt: A stack update must protect an important database from accidental replacement by a routine application change. Which control is relevant?

options.text: Use stack policy or equivalent protected ownership and require an explicit reviewed path for stateful resource changes, with backups and deletion safeguards.
Allow every update to replace the database automatically.
Remove the database from all infrastructure management.
Disable change sets to reduce review time.

feedback.Reason: Stateful resources need stronger update boundaries than frequently changed stateless resources.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Stack policies and resource protection can restrict updates while backups and deletion policies provide recovery depth.
Details.scenarioApplication: The pipeline separates application and database changes and requires an explicit approved migration for a protected resource.
Details.errorCorrection: Automatic replacement risks data loss, removing management loses declared ownership, and disabling review increases risk.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Protection can block a legitimate change, so exceptions need a narrow documented procedure.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Automatic replacement is unsafe for stateful data.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Unmanaged state creates drift and recovery uncertainty.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Less review does not make stateful changes safer.

items.prompt: A recovery pipeline is rerun after a network timeout, and it creates duplicate resources. What property is missing?
constraints: The first operation may have succeeded.

options.text: Use idempotent stack operations, stable names or ownership tags, status reconciliation, and a safe retry policy before starting a second deployment.
Always create a new random stack on every retry.
Delete all resources before each retry without checking state.
Ignore the timeout and assume the operation failed.

feedback.Reason: A timeout is ambiguous; recovery automation must reconcile actual state before repeating an operation.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Idempotent identifiers, stack status, tags, and API reconciliation distinguish an incomplete request from a successful one.
Details.scenarioApplication: The pipeline queries the stack, resumes or updates the existing owner, and cleans up only verified orphan resources.
Details.errorCorrection: Random stacks create duplicates, blind deletion can destroy a successful recovery, and assuming failure compounds the problem.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reconciliation logic adds implementation work but prevents destructive duplicate recovery.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Random names hide ownership and create duplicate capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Blind cleanup can remove a valid partial or complete recovery.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Timeouts do not prove that the service rejected the request.

items.prompt: A team tests a recovery template only through static linting. What additional evidence is needed?
constraints: Static validation does not create resources.
The target Region has different quotas.

options.text: Deploy the template in an isolated target environment, validate dependencies and outputs, exercise the application, and measure cleanup or rollback.
Trust linting because syntax validity proves runtime support.
Run the template in the primary only and assume regional parity.
Skip target deployment to avoid test cost.

feedback.Reason: Static checks catch syntax and some structure, but only a target deployment exposes permissions, quotas, service support, and runtime behavior.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A recovery test exercises resource creation, dependencies, application configuration, and the target Region's operational limits.
Details.scenarioApplication: The team deploys with protected test data, runs representative checks, records timing, and cleans up deliberately.
Details.errorCorrection: Linting cannot prove runtime support, primary success does not prove regional parity, and avoiding tests leaves the path unknown.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Isolated deployments consume cost and quota and need cleanup safeguards.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Syntax validity does not prove resource availability or permissions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Regional capabilities and identifiers can differ.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Cost avoidance does not provide recovery evidence.

items.prompt: A regulated recovery deployment must show who changed the template, which version ran, and what resources changed. Which controls provide this evidence?

options.text: Use version control and approvals for templates, pipeline records for artifacts and actors, CloudFormation stack events, and CloudTrail for API evidence.
Rely on the operator's memory of the deployment.
Keep only the final resource state without change history.
Disable CloudTrail during recovery to reduce noise.

feedback.Reason: Change history and resource events create an auditable chain from approved source to deployed state.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Version control, pipeline metadata, CloudFormation events, and CloudTrail complement one another for source, execution, and API evidence.
Details.scenarioApplication: Auditors can identify the approved template, execution role, target stack, timing, and resulting changes.
Details.errorCorrection: Memory and final state omit history, and disabling audit trails removes evidence during the highest-risk event.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Evidence retention costs storage and needs sensitive-data access controls.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Memory is not reliable or auditable.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Final state does not show who or what caused the change.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Disabling audit during recovery creates a governance blind spot.

items.prompt: A recovery runbook has 35 manual infrastructure steps and operators often skip one under pressure. What is the best improvement?
constraints: Operators still need approval and observation.

options.text: Automate deterministic steps with versioned templates and guarded orchestration, leaving explicit approval and validation gates for high-risk actions.
Add more pages to the runbook without changing execution.
Remove the skipped step from the recovery plan.
Allow operators to run all steps in any order.

feedback.Reason: Automation reduces omission and ordering errors while retaining human control where judgment is required.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Declarative infrastructure and orchestrated dependencies make repeatable operations executable and observable.
Details.scenarioApplication: The pipeline creates resources, waits for readiness, records events, and pauses for data or traffic decisions that need approval.
Details.errorCorrection: More prose does not remove omission, deleting a step hides a dependency, and arbitrary order can fail prerequisites.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Automation needs permissions, rollback, idempotency, and testing; not every judgment should be automated blindly.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: Longer instructions do not guarantee execution fidelity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: Removing a required step makes recovery incomplete.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Dependency order is part of infrastructure correctness.
